newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan bourse finally gets name, trading floor.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan bourse finally gets name, trading floor.

text.p: Uganda's bourse has finally got a name and trading floor and should begin operations in around two weeks, market officials said on Wednesday.

The bourse will be called Uganda Securities Exchange Ltd. Its offices and trading floor will be in the Uganda Commercial Bank building in the capital's commercial district, according to Elly Rwakakooko, chairman of the Stock Exchange Council.
Rwakakooko said all legal formalities had been completed and what remained was the signing of documents to make the company a legal entity which should then start business by latest in mid-May.
"Certainly by mid-May we should have been a legal entity to start business. There now is no impediment," Rwakakooko said.

But market analysts said the new bourse was likely to have little or no business when it opened because the government has sold a controlling shareholding in companies it wanted listed to core investors who may not want to trade the shares.
Uganda's Capital Markets Authority has previously named Uganda Grain Milling Co Ltd, Uganda Consolidated Properties Ltd and National Insurance Corporation as the first to be listed.
That appeared not to be in doubt, said Rwakakooko. In addition a number of private companies had talked to him about possible flotation of part of their shares on the bourse.
"There could be business soon because other than government companies, there are five other companies which want to offload shares on to the market," Rwakakooko told Reuters.
"We are also convincing (the) government to let us trade in government securities, treasury bills and bonds," he added.

Last month, the Capital Markets Authority licensed seven brokerage companies -- African Alliance Uganda Ltd, PMC (MBEA) Investment Ltd, Stanbic International, Dyer & Blair, Greenland Finance, Crane Financial Services and Uganda Commercial Bank.
Rwakakooko did not give an indication of which companies were expected to be the first to be listed on the securities exchange or what levels of growth were anticipated.
